sections.text: Introduction

This method is applicable to the routine 
determination of various form of phosphorus in waters containing from 0.1 to 3 
mg/L (ppm) of phosphorus. When modified by the addition of bismuth salt to the 
acid reagent, it is applicable to waters containing 0.03 to 1 mg/L of 
phosphorus. The ranges, which can be extended upward by diluting a smaller 
aliquot to the prescribed volume, are for photometric measurements in a 20 mm 
cell.

The first draft was initiated by chemist: Salwa 
Ebraheem EL-Desoky; reviewed by department director chemist: Hoda Hasaneen; 
revised by quality control chemist: Mohamed Mosbah Mokpel, and accepted by eng.Fathy 
Mahmoud Ragab, 
and approved by Eng: Awad M. Fatthy; Head Sector 
of Talkha Power Station.

This document is accepted by eng. Samir 
Abd El Gilil EDEPC MPIS coordinator, and certified by accountant; Mahmoud 
Mohamed Soliman; EDEPC admin and financial inspection, quality control General 
Director and supervisor of inspection and quality control head sector.
Significance and Uses

Phosphorus is widely 
distributed in the environment as both inorganic and organically bound 
phosphates. Sources of phosphates include surface-applied fertilizers, cleaning and 
laundering products, boiler water conditioners, and drinking water treatment aids. Because phosphorus is a nutrient for 
photosynthetic organisms it may be important to monitor and control discharge 
into the environment.
Summary

Orthophosphate reacts with ammonium molybdate in 
an acid medium to form a molybdophosphate that in turn is reduced to a 
molybdenum blue complex with amino-naphthol-sulfonic acid. The color is 
proportional in intensity to the phosphorus concentration. When Bismuth salt is 
added to the sulfuric acid reagent, the intensity of the blue color developed in 
the test is increased about fourfold. Only orthophosphate forms a blue color in 
the test. Other forms of phosphorus such as polyphosphate and organic phosphorus 
compounds can be converted to orthophosphate by the various sample digestive treatments 
prescribed in the method.
Sampling

The sample must be taken as the 
applicable ASTM methods D 3370 76.

When determining only dissolved 
phosphorus, filter the sample through a 0.45-m membrane filter after sampling.

Analysis is best performed immediately after collecting the sample to minimize 
possible change.

Preserve the sample by adding 40 mg of mercuric chloride per litre of sample and 
refrigerating it at 4oC 
if analysis can't be performed at the same day of collecting, and to prevent 
precipitation of the mercury, previously add sufficient sodium chloride to the 
sample, if necessary, so that chloride content will be at least 50 mg/L in the 
sample.

If total recoverable phosphorus only is to be determined preservation isn't 
needed.
Sample storage in glass bottles is suggested.
Interferences

Up to 40 mg/l (ppm) 
of iron, 75mg/L of chromate and 50,000 mg/l of chloride will not interfere 
with 
the test.

If more then than 75mg/L of chromate 
is present in the sample, the reference solution for the photometric measurement should not be 
water instead It must be the sample treated with all reagents except the molybdate 
solution.

No more than 1500 mg/L of chloride 
should be present in the sample when the bismuth modification is followed.

sections.text: Safety Precautions

Make sure that the sample 
bottle is correctly labeled.

Make sure that the sample bottle is 
free from dust and dirt.

The sample must be kept away 
from exposure to direct sunlight.

Cleaning solvents such as acid dichromate, 
nitric acid and others are dangerous, so you have to wear breathing mask.

Keep this solvents closed. Do not get 
it in the eyes, on the skin, or on clothing. Do not breath them, use only in a 
hood.

sections.text: Reagent

Amino Solution 
Dissolve in 100 ml of water the following chemicals in given order; 3.7 g of 
sodium sulfite(Na2SO3), 0.1g of 1-amino 2-naphthol 4sulfonic acid, and 6.2 g of sodium metabisulfite ( sodium pyrosulfite, Na2S2O5 
). Store the solution in an amber bottle and make it up fresh every 2 weeks.

Ammonium Molybdate 
Solution (48g/L) Dissolve 48g of ammonium molybdate 
[(NH4)6Mo7O24 .4H2O] 
in about 800 ml of water. Add 2.5 ml of ammonium hydroxide (NH4OH, sp 
gr 0.90) and dilute it to 1 L with water.

Ammonium 
Persulfate- Crystalline ammonium persulfate ((NH4)2S2O8). 
Potassium persulfate ( K2S2O8) is a suitable 
replacement for the ammonium salt.

Phosphorus Standard 
Solution (1ml = 0.025mg of phosphorus ) First prepare a stock solution (1 ml = 
0.05 mg of phosphorus) by dissolving in water 0.2197 g of potassium dihydrogen 
phosphate (KH2PO4) that has been dried for 1 h in an oven 
at 105oC, and diluting the solution to exactly 1 L with water. 
Prepare the standard solution by diluting 50.0 ml of the stock solution to 100 
ml with water in a volumetric flask.

Sulfuric Acid 
(37+63) Add 370 ml of concentrated sulfuric acid (H2SO4,sp 
gr 1.842) slowly to about 600 ml of water. Cool and dilute it to 1L with water.

Sulfuric Acid ( 
37+63, Bismuth added )- Dissolve 1.200 g of bismuth nitrate (Bi(NO3)3.5H2O) 
in 250 ml of H2SO4 (37+63) while still warm.

sections.text: Work to be Carried out
Calibration
For a range from 0.1 to 3 mg/L (ppm)

Prepare a series of standard 
phosphate solutions to cover the range from 0 to 3 mg / L. Make up the 
standards by diluting suitable volumes of phosphorus standard solution (1 ml = 
0.025 mg of phosphorus ) to 100 ml with water.

Develop color in the series 
of standards as directed in the following procedure (part 1).

Measure the absorbance of 
each standard at 650 nm in a 20-mm cell using water as the reference solution 
for the initial photometer setting to zero. Plot the absorbance value as the 
ordinate and the corresponding phosphorus concentrations as the abscissa on 
linear graph paper.

sections.text: Procedure
Part 1

a) Orthophosphate, Range from 
0.1 to 3 mg/L of phosphorus

Transfer 100 ml of 
the clear sample containing 3mg /l of phosphorus or less into a 250 ml 
Erlenmeyer flask. For higher concentrations use a smaller sample and dilute it 
to 100 ml with water. 
Note: Filtering the sample through a 0.45 m membrane filter will normally remove 
particulate matter for the determination of dissolved orthophosphate in boiler 
waters. However, even a retentative filter paper may not be satisfactory if the 
boiler contains a dispersive. If a filter paper is to be used, add 4 g of 
potassium nitrate (KNO3) and 2 to 4 ml of sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl) solution 
and boil it several minutes to flocculate the precipitated matter before 
filtering.

Add the following 
reagents in the given order to the sample, mixing after each addition: 5 ml of 
H2SO4 (37+63), 5 ml of ammonium Molybdate solution, and 
5 ml of amino solution, allow no less than 9 min, nor more than (11 min) for 
color development.

Measure the 
absorbance of the test sample at 650 nm, employing water as the reference 
solution. When the chromate is higher than 75 mg/L in the sample analyzed use 
the method described in interference section before. Record the milligrams per litre of phosphorus indicated by the calibration curve established before.

sections.text:
(b) Hydrolysable Phosphorus + 
Orthophosphate, Range from 0.1 to 3 mg/L of Phosphorus

Proceed 
in accordance with part 1a.

Add 5ml of H2SO4,(37+63) to the sample, use 7 ml of concentrated 
hydrochloric acid (HCl, 
sp gr 1.19) instead of 5 ml of H2SO4 (37+63) if the calcium 
in the sample is more than 200 mg/l. Boil the solution for at least 30 min on a 
hot plate, adding water to keep the volume between 25 to 100 ml, alternatively, 
heat the solution for 10 min in an autoclave or pressure cooker at 103 to 138 
kPa (15 to 20 psi). Cool the solution to about 25oC (77oF). 
Do not over chill. Dilute the solution to 105 ml with water by means of a plastic 
graduated cylinder having a mark at the 105-ml level.

Add 5 ml of 
ammonium Molybdate solution and 5 ml of amino solution, mixing after each 
addition. Allow no less than 9 min, nor more than 11 min for color development.

Measure the 
absorbance of the test sample at 650 nm to obtain hydrolysable phosphorus + 
orthophosphate.

sections.text: Calculation

Calculate the 
concentration of the various form of phosphorus in milligrams per liter

( parts 
per million ) of phosphorus by applying the following equation for 
orthophosphate determined in part 1 and part 2.

Orthophosphate, mg/l of 
phosphorus = A (100/B)
Where:

A = milligrams per 
liter of phosphorus indicated by the calibration curve.

B = 
milliliters of sample analyzed.

Hydrolyzable Phosphorus = ( Hydrolyzable Phosphorus + Orthophosphate Phosphorus) (Orthophosphate 
Phosphorus)
Particulate Phosphorus = (Total Recoverable Phosphorus) (Total Dissolved Phosphorus)

SO = singleoperator precision , mg/L

a = 
concentration of phosphate determined, mg/L and

Procedure
Part 1
a) Orthophosphate, Range from 
0.1 to 3 mg/L of phosphorus
Transfer 100 ml of 
the clear sample containing 3mg /l of phosphorus or less into a 250 ml 
Erlenmeyer flask. For higher concentrations use a smaller sample and dilute it 
to 100 ml with water. 
Note: Filtering the sample through a 0.45 m membrane filter will normally remove 
particulate matter for the determination of dissolved orthophosphate in boiler 
waters. However, even a retentative filter paper may not be satisfactory if the 
boiler contains a dispersive. If a filter paper is to be used, add 4 g of 
potassium nitrate (KNO3) and 2 to 4 ml of sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl) solution 
and boil it several minutes to flocculate the precipitated matter before 
filtering.
Add the following 
reagents in the given order to the sample, mixing after each addition: 5 ml of 
H2SO4 (37+63), 5 ml of ammonium Molybdate solution, and 
5 ml of amino solution, allow no less than 9 min, nor more than (11 min) for 
color development.
Measure the 
absorbance of the test sample at 650 nm, employing water as the reference 
solution. When the chromate is higher than 75 mg/L in the sample analyzed use 
the method described in interference section before. Record the milligrams per litre of phosphorus indicated by the calibration curve established before.

Calculation
Calculate the 
concentration of the various form of phosphorus in milligrams per liter
( parts 
per million ) of phosphorus by applying the following equation for 
orthophosphate determined in part 1 and part 2.
Orthophosphate, mg/l of 
phosphorus = A (100/B)
Where:
A = milligrams per 
liter of phosphorus indicated by the calibration curve.
B = 
milliliters of sample analyzed.
Hydrolyzable Phosphorus = ( Hydrolyzable Phosphorus + Orthophosphate Phosphorus) (Orthophosphate 
Phosphorus)
Organic Phosphorus = (Total 
Recoverable Phosphate) ( HydrolyzablePhosphorus + Orthophosphate Phosphorus 
)
Particulate Phosphorus = (Total Recoverable Phosphorus) (Total Dissolved Phosphorus)
Precision
The precision of the method 
for dissolved orthophosphate:
In the range from 0.1 to 3 mg/L of phosphorus can 
be expressed as follows:
ST = 0.65 a / S, 
and
SO = 
(0.52 a + 0.55) / S
In the range from 0.03 to 1 mg/L of phosphorus, 
the precision is:
ST =(1.4 a 
0.31) / S and
SO = (0.31 a) / S
Where:
ST = overall precision , mg/L
SO = singleoperator precision , mg/L
a = 
concentration of phosphate determined, mg/L and
